### Pain — radial, ulnar or central?
- Divide wrist pain first: radial side or ulnar side (Kasr Al-Ainy)

|---|---|

| Central | Kienböck disease, SL (scapholunate) or LT (lunotriquetral) dissociation, perilunate injury |

|---|---|

| Punching a hard object | little finger metacarpal neck fracture |
| Ball hits the fingertip | mallet finger |
| Thumb forced away (skiing) | thumb ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) tear |
| Hand used as a hammer | hook of hamate fracture |

| Weak grip | pain or real weakness? |

| Stiffness | which daily task fails? |
| Night pain and tingling | carpal tunnel syndrome (→ ch 5) |

- "Sitting face to face, both upper limbs bared above the elbows."

### The route on one page
| Position | What you do (in order) |
|---|---|
| Sitting | Set-up: face to face, both limbs bared, hands on a pillow |
| Sitting | Look: five screening positions, then four sides |
| Sitting | Feel: temperature; landmarks radial → central → ulnar → palm |
| Sitting | Move: wrist, forearm rotation, fingers, thumb |
| Sitting | Measure: grip, pinch, tip-to-palm distance |
| Sitting | Tendons: FDP, FDS, EPL, extensor lag, tenodesis (4.3) |
| Sitting | Special: tests chosen by the tender spot (4.4) |
| Finish | nerve screen, pulses, Allen, elbow, shoulder, neck |

- **Memory:** Look, Feel, Move, Measure, Special; then Neuro, Vascular, Joints above

### Set-up
- Patient sitting facing you, about 60 cm away; watch the face while you feel
- Both limbs bared above the elbows; one rolled sleeve is not accepted (Kasr Al-Ainy)

### Look
#### Screening — five positions
| Position | Look for |
|---|---|
| Palms up | arcade, thenar and hypothenar wasting |
| Fist, palms up | tips reach the palm; fingers point to the scaphoid tubercle |
| Palms down | nails, joint swellings, ganglion, guttering |
| Fist, palms down | knuckle line, MCP swelling, dropped finger |
| Elbows up | elbow nodules, plaques, scars |

- MCP = metacarpophalangeal; PIP / DIP = proximal / distal interphalangeal

#### Look from each side
- **Memory:** at every side think **DCS** — deformity, contour and wasting, skin

| Side | Look for |
|---|---|
| Palm | Dupuytren nodules and cords |
| Radial | thumb alignment, squared thumb base, snuffbox fullness |
| Dorsum | nodes, synovitis, caput ulnae |
| Ulnar | hypothenar, little finger flexion |

### Feel
- Back of the hand for temperature; then find one tender spot

|---|---|---|

| Radial | snuffbox, scaphoid tubercle | scaphoid fracture or non-union |
| Radial | trapezium, thumb CMC | CMC OA |
| Central | just distal to Lister's tubercle | SL ligament; dorsal ganglion |
| Ulnar | ulnar head | DRUJ arthritis or instability |
| Ulnar | soft spot distal to the ulnar head | TFCC (fovea sign, 4.4) |

4.03.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you test the tendons?"
- "Look at the arcade first; then test each tendon alone."
- "FDP: hold the PIP straight. FDS: hold the other fingers straight."
- "Dropped finger: passive extension held? Tenodesis intact? Then rupture or palsy."

### Flexors
#### FDP test
- **Aim:** flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) of one finger
- **How:** hold the PIP straight; "bend the last joint of your finger"
- **Positive:** no DIP flexion → FDP cut or avulsed
- **Why:** FDP is the only flexor of the DIP joint
- **Trap:** plain words, not muscle names (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- **Video:** [▶ openmichigan · 0:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ahwXumsN7d4)

[[FIG: Fig 4.13 — FDP: PIP held, the fingertip bends · 4.03

#### FDS test
- **Aim:** flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) of one finger
- **How:** hold the other fingers straight; patient bends the free finger
- **Positive:** no PIP flexion → FDS cut
- **Why:** all FDP tendons share one belly; holding the others blocks FDP
- **Trap:** with FDS working, the fingertip stays floppy
- **Video:** [▶ EM:RAP Medical Education · 1:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fns_fpSF_ys)

[[FIG: Fig 4.14 — FDS: other fingers held straight, PIP bends · 4.03

- Jersey finger: FDP avulsion, ring finger lies straight in the arcade
- Both tendons cut → both IP joints straight; FDS alone → slight break only
[[FIG: Fig 4.15 — FDP avulsion; both flexors cut in the index · 4.03

| Flexor pollicis longus (FPL) | Point |
|---|---|
| Test | hold the MCP; "bend the thumb tip" |
| No IP flexion | FPL rupture (Mannerfelt lesion in RA) |
| Differential | trigger thumb; anterior interosseous nerve palsy |

### Extensors
#### EPL (retropulsion) test
- **Aim:** extensor pollicis longus (EPL)
- **How:** hand flat on the table; patient lifts the thumb off it
- **Positive:** cannot lift → EPL rupture (radius fracture, plate, RA)
- **Why:** retropulsion isolates EPL; EPB alone cannot do it (Campbell)
- **Video:** [▶ Sarah Tucker Oxford · 1:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hY3QKtVFtg)

[[FIG: Fig 4.16 — Thumb attitude in EPL rupture; EPL tested in isolation · 4.03

- EPL rupture → extensor indicis transfer; check it is present

#### Extensor lag
- **Aim:** active extension lost, joint free
- **How:** you extend the finger passively; patient holds it there
- **Positive:** finger drops; passive more than active → tendon rupture
- **Why:** the joint moves, so the motor is missing
- **Trap:** also MCP subluxation, sagittal band tear, PIN palsy
- **Video:** [▶ Arthritis Research Canada · 0:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AQ0f7MHmu8A)

[[FIG: Fig 4.17 — Dropped ring finger: extensor rupture over a caput ulnae · 4.03

- RA ruptures little, then ring, then middle extensor → Vaughan-Jackson syndrome

### Tenodesis
#### Tenodesis test
- **Aim:** tendon continuity without patient effort
- **How:** you extend the wrist passively, then flex it
- **Positive:** finger does not flex on wrist extension → flexor cut
- **Why:** wrist extension tightens an intact flexor
- **Trap:** fingers dropped, tenodesis normal → PIN palsy (Exam Techniques)
- **Video:** [▶ Dalhousie Plastic Surgery · 2:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=imPQve7ZL3o)

[[FIG: Fig 4.18 — Wrist extension flexes the fingers; flexion extends them · 4.03

#### Other tendon signs
| Sign | Point |
|---|---|
| Index and little extensor check | other MCPs flexed; index or little still extends |
| Quadriga effect | one FDP stuck → others cannot fully flex |
| Lumbrical plus | flexion → paradoxical PIP extension |
| Linburg sign | thumb flexed; index cannot extend → FPL–FDP slip |

- EPB = extensor pollicis brevis; PIN = posterior interosseous nerve

PITFALL — "every dropped finger is a ruptured tendon"
- PIN palsy, MCP subluxation and sagittal band tears look the same
- Say → "**Passive extension is held and tenodesis works, so the tendon is intact.**"

### Is the scaphoid broken?
#### Anatomical snuffbox tenderness
- **Aim:** scaphoid waist fracture or non-union
- **How:** patient lifts the thumb; you press the hollow
- **Positive:** tender against the sound side → scaphoid fracture or non-union
- **Why:** the scaphoid waist is the floor of the snuffbox
- **Trap:** press the tubercle too; styloid lies just proximal (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- **Video:** [▶ JJ Medicine · 1:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TCDluv83TpE)

[[FIG: Fig 4.19 — Snuffbox palpation in course case 1; snuffbox borders · 4.04

- Snuffbox borders: EPL dorsal; abductor pollicis longus (APL) and EPB volar

#### Scaphoid compression test
- **Aim:** scaphoid fracture, non-union or scaphoid arthritis
- **How:** push the thumb metacarpal along its axis toward the scaphoid
